subject.title: Subagent Premature Announce Bug - Model-Specific Tool Call Handling Issues

question: Should OpenClaw promote provider-specific tagged tool-call markers found inside reasoning/thinking content into executable tool calls, and what validation boundary should own that behavior?
rationale: The code path is clear enough to show why current main misses the markers, but executing tool calls recovered from reasoning text changes the security boundary and needs maintainer intent plus live provider proof.

options.title: Approve gated provider normalization
options.body: Allow a provider-owned Qwen/ModelStudio parser, or a narrow shared helper, only for standalone validated marker blocks whose tool names are in the request's allowed tool set, with live provider proof before merge.

options.title: Require more live evidence first
options.body: Keep the issue open with no fix PR until maintainers or the reporter provide a current-main Qwen/ModelStudio transcript that reproduces the thinking-only marker output.

options.title: Do not execute reasoning markers
options.body: Document the affected model/provider combinations as unsupported for tool use and keep using working alternatives such as qwen3.5-plus rather than parsing hidden reasoning text.

recommendation.title: Approve gated provider normalization
recommendation.body: Allow a provider-owned Qwen/ModelStudio parser, or a narrow shared helper, only for standalone validated marker blocks whose tool names are in the request's allowed tool set, with live provider proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a maintainer-level product/security boundary choice, and steipete is the clearest available routing signal from the issue timeline and adjacent provider/runtime work.
